packageRules.description: The requirements in manifest.json change the code that runs in Home Assistant: merged by hand, and shipped only with a release.
prBodyNotes: This changes what Home Assistant installs. Check that it fits the packages Home Assistant pins (`homeassistant/package_constraints.txt`) in the oldest version supported in `hacs.json`, merge it by hand after reading the changelog, and ship it with a release (bump `version` in `manifest.json`).

packageRules.description: What the app's image installs, and the image it starts from, change the code that searches: merged by hand, and shipped only with a release of the app. fast-flights builds the Google Flights search: try a real search before releasing it.
prBodyNotes: This changes what the app runs. Merge it by hand after reading the changelog (for `fast-flights`, after a real search), and ship it with a release: bump `version` in `app/config.yaml` and in `manifest.json` together.

packageRules.description: Test tools merge themselves when the tests pass.
GitHub Actions in one pull request, merged by themselves when the tests pass unless one of them has a new major version.
Actions are pinned to a commit (helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests), so a moved tag or branch cannot change what runs. Pins and their updates merge themselves when the tests pass.

hassfest and the HACS action follow their branch, as their docs say: they check against today's rules of Home Assistant and HACS, their tagged releases are years old, and both run a Docker image that follows the branch, so a pinned commit would not freeze what runs. The workflow can only read the repository.
The Python of the tests follows the one Home Assistant runs on, not the newest release: changed by hand.
